newsitem.title: USA: CRSS discussing New England acquisitions.
newsitem.headline: CRSS discussing New England acquisitions.

text.p: Tractebel SA's CRSS Inc is discussing the acquisition of New England power plants, chief executive William P. Utt told Reuters.

He said the company is interested in acquiring generating capacity in the U.S. Northeast and has discussed the purchase of plants owned by Commonwealth Energy System and Boston Edison Co, which have announced plans to sell their generating capacity to meet requirements set by Massachusetts officials.
The company "can not comment" on any contacts with New England Electric System, he said.
Utt said this is because of confidentiality requirements imposed by NEES, which has invited a "select group" to bid on its power plants.

He said CRSS' 30 megawatt cogeneration plant in Westwood, Pa, has received an offer from GPU Inc as part of the utility's program to spend up to $1 billion to buy out or buy down Pennsylvania independent power producer contracts.
Utt declined to discuss the GPU offer.

He said the company has varying interests in 18 U.S. and Canadian power projects capable of generating 1,870.8 megawatts of power and 877.3 thermal megawatts. Sixteen of these, including two in Canada, are in operation and two under development.
Utt said the 18 have total assets of $2.2 billion.
All but one of the 14 in operation in the U.S. are operated and controlled by CRSS, he said, noting five are in New England, three in Pennsylvania, and two each in Michigan and Virginia.
Utt also said the company is working on a name change this week to better identify it as a Tractebel unit, adding an announcement is planned this month.
